title: Silas and the Debt
premise: Paloma Ashgrove, a freelance interpreter who quietly handles the delegations and disputes governments prefer to deny, receives a call on a burner phone from her mentor Tomas Veyra—a man officially dead for two years. He claims the peace accord she is about to interpret was engineered to collapse, and that a hidden annex proves three governments conspired with the assassin known as Corvus to guarantee it. As Paloma smuggles the annex through checkpoints, betrayals, and Corvus's tightening hunt, she gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced archivist, a defected driver, and a teenage courier. In the end she trades her own anonymity—her only protection—for a public reading of the annex at the failed summit's reopening, exposing the conspiracy at the cost of Tomas's life and her old identity, but winning justice the law could never deliver.
about_author: Dominic Coldharbour is the pen name of a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade in rooms where nothing said was meant to be heard. He writes thrillers about the people history forgets to credit—and sometimes forgets to protect.

chapters.title: The Voice That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Arriving in Geneva for a fragile truce summit, Paloma answers a burner phone slipped into her coat: it's Tomas Veyra, her mentor, dead two years by official record. He warns the accord will fail by design and hangs up. The beat is vertigo—the safe, invisible life she built cracks open in a single ring.

chapters.title: Interpreting the Lie
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. During opening sessions, Paloma notices deliberate mistranslations steering both delegations toward rupture. She tests a delegate with a subtle error and confirms someone inside is sabotaging talks. Emotional beat: professional dread hardening into resolve; she realizes her skill itself has made her dangerous.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: POV alternating Paloma and the assassin Corvus, who has been contracted to ensure the summit collapses and to erase anyone holding the annex. Corvus identifies Paloma as a thread to pull. The beat is cold menace: we see how methodically the machinery of 'accident' is assembled around her.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Basement
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Following Tomas's clues, she finds Mirela Okonkwo, a disgraced treaty archivist living off-grid beneath a shuttered records office. Mirela confirms the annex exists—but it's split across three sealed national archives. Beat: wary alliance; two invisible women choosing to be seen together.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Carries Everything
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A teenage courier named Denny, who once ran messages for Tomas, becomes their link between cities. Corvus's surveillance closes in; they relocate twice in one night. Beat: found family forming under pressure—Paloma discovering she can protect people instead of merely translating them.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Their driver, Ferenc, is offered immunity to betray them and takes the first fragment of the annex to his old intelligence handlers. Paloma must decide whether to hunt him or trust him to double-cross his handlers. Beat: loyalty versus truth made literal; she chooses trust and loses the fragment.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in the Rain
chapters.summary: POV Corvus. Corvus intercepts the fragment, kills the handler, and finally meets Paloma face-to-face—offering her a walk-away. She refuses, and he lets her go, unsettled by something Tomas once told him. Beat: the hunter revealed as another man trapped in the machinery; moral fault lines deepen.

chapters.title: Tomas's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A rendezvous with Tomas reveals he faked his death to infiltrate the conspiracy—and that he recruited Corvus years ago. He gives her the final key to the annex, then is mortally wounded covering their escape. Beat: grief fused with purpose; the mentor's last lesson is sacrifice over survival.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Room
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. With Mirela's archive access, Denny's smuggling routes, and even Ferenc's redemption, the team reassembles the full annex hours before the summit's ceremonial reopening. Corvus, having read what Tomas left him, stands down rather than fire. Climax beat: every piece of the found family pays off at once.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Seizing the interpreter's microphone, Paloma reads the annex aloud to delegates and live feeds, burning her cover name forever. Governments scramble, the sabotage is exposed, and Corvus vanishes into the crowd—alive, changed. Resolution beat: justice outside the law, purchased with anonymity; Paloma walks out unnamed but no longer invisible where it matters.
